qAndA.answer: Skanda Prasad draws diagonals in the square and uses the Pythagorean theorem to calculate the length of the diagonals. He then divides the diagonal length by 2 to find the distance from the charges to the center.
qAndA.question: How does Skanda Prasad find the distance from the charges to the center of the square in the second problem?

qAndA.answer: The value of the charge that must be placed at the fourth corner of the square to make the net potential at the center zero is -12 microcoulombs (µC).

Anand reminds viewers that he has started a physics series.

Anand asks viewers to like and subscribe to his own channel.

activities.description: Skanda Prasad starts writing on a whiteboard.
Skanda Prasad draws and points at the whiteboard.

narrativeProgression.description: Skanda Prasad introduces two physics problems based on electrostatics and electric potential.
Skanda Prasad begins to solve the first problem by drawing a diagram and explaining the given information.
Skanda Prasad writes the formulas for calculating electric potential.
Skanda Prasad sets up the equation for finding the point where electric potential is zero.
Skanda Prasad solves for the distance and finds the answer to the first problem.
Skanda Prasad moves on to the second problem.
Skanda Prasad draws a square to represent the problem and marks the charges at three corners.
Skanda Prasad draws diagonals and calculates the distance from the charges to the center of the square.
Skanda Prasad sets up the equation for finding the charge at the fourth corner that would make the net potential at the center zero.
Skanda Prasad simplifies the equation and solves for the charge, finding the answer to the second problem.
Skanda Prasad thanks Anand for the opportunity to be on his channel and thanks the viewers for watching.
